column4: The Creator who "created everything" then فَقَدَّرَهُ تَقْدِيرًا states outright the section's sequence from crafting to exact measure.
إِنَّا كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلَقْنَاهُ بِقَدَرٍ joins خ ل ق and ق د ر in one claim: every created thing already bears a measure.
أَلَمْ نَخْلُقكُّم answers the section's "did We not make" stance by confronting humans with their crafted origin in a lowly fluid.
فَجَعَلْنَاهُ فِى قَرَارٍ مَّكِينٍ supplies the bodily scene behind 77:20: the created drop is placed in a secure womb, so جعل is concrete fitting and placement.
إِلَىٰ قَدَرٍ مَّعْلُومٍ gives the womb-stage a known limit, the section's sense of a thing being carried to its appointed boundary.
فَقَدَرْنَا فَنِعْمَ ٱلْقَادِرُونَ lets the same root name divine determining and divine ability, exactly the double hearing developed in the section.
ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ presents creation as proportioning and setting straight, matching الخلق as "straight measure."
وَٱلَّذِى قَدَّرَ فَهَدَىٰ makes measure lead to guidance, the same creation–measure–two-path sequence the section finds across 90:4-10.
Moses identifies the Lord as the One who أَعْطَىٰ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلْقَهُۥ ثُمَّ هَدَىٰ: each thing receives its fitted creation and then its way.
مِن نُّطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُۥ فَقَدَّرَهُۥ places the human himself under the two acts—created from a drop, then measured—before he can presume autonomy.
قَدْ جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدْرًا combines جعل with a divinely set measure for every thing, and says that unexpected provision also lies within that measure.
Jonah's فَظَنَّ أَن لَّن نَّقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ reproduces the section's ظن/لن/نقدر/عليه pattern; his call from the darkness shows mistaken reckoning yielding to return.
أَيَحْسَبُ ٱلْإِنسَانُ أَلَّن نَّجْمَعَ عِظَامَهُۥ repeats the interrogative supposition and makes its object a false limit placed on God's power.
بَلَىٰ قَادِرِينَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّسَوِّىَ بَنَانَهُۥ answers 75:3 with power to refashion even fingertips, making divine ability an exact bodily proportioning.
أَيَحْسَبُ ٱلْإِنسَانُ أَن يُتْرَكَ سُدًى asks whether the human supposes he will be left unmeasured and without a claim upon him.
فَخَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ grounds the rebuke of 75:36 in the human's having been created and proportioned.
فَجَعَلَ مِنْهُ ٱلزَّوْجَيْنِ continues the crafted-body argument through the making of the two sexes, joining جعل to birth.
أَلَيْسَ ذَٰلِكَ بِقَادِرٍ closes the creation scene by asking whether its Maker has power to restore the dead; created measure is evidence of power.
نَحْنُ خَلَقْنَاكُمْ فَلَوْلَا تُصَدِّقُونَ makes "We created you" the answer to human denial, the stance underlying the section's measured human.
ءَأَنتُمْ تَخْلُقُونَهُۥٓ أَمْ نَحْنُ ٱلْخَالِقُونَ excludes human ownership of his own formation and assigns the craft to God.
نَحْنُ قَدَّرْنَا بَيْنَكُمُ ٱلْمَوْتَ makes death itself an allotment "among you," joining measurement, division, and the limit no human escapes.
عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّبَدِّلَ أَمْثَٰلَكُمْ completes 56:60 by naming the bodily replacement God's allotment cannot be prevented from accomplishing.
After measuring what wombs lose and gain, the ayah says وَكُلُّ شَىْءٍ عِندَهُۥ بِمِقْدَارٍ; birth and every thing have a known extent with God.
Water descends بِقَدَرٍ while God is عَلَىٰ ذَهَابٍۭ بِهِۦ لَقَٰدِرُونَ, setting measured provision and sovereign ability side by side in one scene.
وَقَدَّرَ فِيهَآ أَقْوَٰتَهَا apportions the earth's sustenance, a direct cosmic instance of the section's measured share.
وَقَدِّرْ فِى ٱلسَّرْدِ commands David to measure the links while making armor, a literal artisan use of ق د ر like laying out leather before cutting.
God جَعَلَ night for rest and the sun and moon حُسْبَانًا, then calls their courses تَقْدِيرُ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْعَلِيمِ; making, calculation, and measure meet.
وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلنُّجُومَ لِتَهْتَدُوا۟ continues 6:96 from measured heavenly signs to guidance, paralleling "measured, then guided."
The moon is given measured stations so people know عَدَدَ ٱلسِّنِينَ وَٱلْحِسَابَ, while مَا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ ذَٰلِكَ إِلَّا بِٱلْحَقِّ joins creation to true counting.
وَٱللَّهُ يُقَدِّرُ ٱلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ عَلِمَ أَن لَّن تُحْصُوهُ contrasts God's measuring with humans' inability to count the measure fully.
the wealth-hoarder جَمَعَ مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ supplies the section's concrete alternative to mere supposition: he counts and recounts the wealth on which he relies.
يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُۥٓ أَخْلَدَهُۥ turns that counting into a false supposition that wealth defeats his appointed limit.
إِنَّهُۥ فَكَّرَ وَقَدَّرَ is the Qur'an's exact instance of the dictionary sense "the human considers the matter and measures it."
فَقُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ condemns the man's self-made estimate, exposing a human use of measure set against the Creator's true measure.
ثُمَّ قُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ repeats the condemnation and makes the failure of his calculation, rather than mere thought, the passage's emphasis.
The tested human treats generous provision as the verdict رَبِّىٓ أَكْرَمَنِ, supplying the first half of the false human reading whose second half is 89:16.
فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُۥ gives the exact "provision was narrowed for him" sense named in the section, while the human wrongly calls the measure humiliation.
The garden owners أَقْسَمُوا۟ لَيَصْرِمُنَّهَا turn oath into a plan to cut the crop, concretely joining قسم, human calculation, and presumed control.
أَن لَّا يَدْخُلَنَّهَا ٱلْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكُم مِّسْكِينٌ reveals what their measured plan withholds: the poor person's share.
وَغَدَوْا۟ عَلَىٰ حَرْدٍ قَٰدِرِينَ depicts them setting out convinced of their capacity, the garden-story equivalent of "none can have power over me."
بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ reverses their plan: those who meant to deprive the poor discover that their own allotted portion has been withheld.
أَهُمْ يَقْسِمُونَ رَحْمَتَ رَبِّكَ is answered by نَحْنُ قَسَمْنَا بَيْنَهُم مَّعِيشَتَهُمْ, distinguishing human claims to divide from God's apportionment of livelihood.
Humans جَعَلُوا۟ ... نَصِيبًا for God and partners بِزَعْمِهِمْ; their invented partition opposes the Creator's measured share and rests on mere claim.
مَا لَهُۥ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَٰقٍ uses the section's named derivative خلاق in its exact sense "allotted share," here a share forfeited in the hereafter.
The person who asks only for this world has وَمَا لَهُۥ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَٰقٍ, showing خلاق as a measured portion rather than creation.
Those who trade God's covenant and their oaths لَا خَلَٰقَ لَهُمْ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ, bringing oath and the derivative meaning "share" into one judgment.
فَٱسْتَمْتَعُوا۟ بِخَلَٰقِهِمْ ... بِخَلَٰقِكُمْ uses خلاق twice for each people's allotted worldly portion and warns against mistaking that portion for immunity.
قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ lets أَحَد name the One whom the man's negative "no one" leaves out of account.
لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ places the One beyond the begetting and being begotten sworn by in 90:3, separating Creator from the created lineage.
وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ is the true absolute negative with أَحَد: no one is His equal, unlike the human's imagined invulnerability.
لَّا يُعَذِّبُ عَذَابَهُۥٓ أَحَدٌ reverses the boast: on that day "no one" can punish as God punishes.
وَلَا يُوثِقُ وَثَاقَهُۥٓ أَحَدٌ completes the reversal with a binding no one can match, the ultimate limit placed on the self-assured man.
The jinn conclude أَن لَّن نُّعْجِزَ ٱللَّهَ ... وَلَن نُّعْجِزَهُۥ هَرَبًا: neither earthly position nor flight puts anyone beyond God's power.
قُلْ إِنِّى لَن يُجِيرَنِى مِنَ ٱللَّهِ أَحَدٌ makes the "len ... ahad" construction confess the opposite truth: no one can shelter even the speaker from God.
وَلَا يَحْسَبَنَّ ... سَبَقُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُمْ لَا يُعْجِزُونَ forbids the thought that wrongdoers have outrun the One who can seize them.
لَا تَحْسَبَنَّ ... مُعْجِزِينَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ directly couples false supposition with the imagined ability to frustrate God's power.
أَمْ حَسِبَ ... أَن يَسْبِقُونَا asks whether evildoers calculate that they can get ahead of God, a precise parallel to imagined unreachability.
خَلَقَ ٱلْإِنسَانَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ establishes the created human origin that makes the later self-sufficient posture in this passage absurd.
كَلَّآ إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَانَ لَيَطْغَىٰ names the transgression that follows when a created human mistakes his allotted condition for autonomy.
أَن رَّءَاهُ ٱسْتَغْنَىٰ says he transgresses because he sees himself as self-sufficient, the inner premise of "no one has power over me."
إِنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلرُّجْعَىٰ gives that self-sufficient human his actual endpoint and owner.
أَلَمْ يَعْلَم بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرَىٰ directly answers the human's supposition that no one saw him.
إِنَّهُۥ ظَنَّ أَن لَّن يَحُورَ repeats ظن and لن in a false belief that the prosperous person will never return.
بَلَىٰٓ إِنَّ رَبَّهُۥ كَانَ بِهِۦ بَصِيرًا answers 84:14 through the Lord's seeing, joining mistaken immunity to the section's second "does he think no one saw him?"
أَمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّا لَا نَسْمَعُ سِرَّهُمْ asks whether hidden plotters suppose they go unheard, then says the messengers beside them write it down.
They ظَنُّوٓا۟ their fortresses would protect them from God, but He came مِنْ حَيْثُ لَمْ يَحْتَسِبُوا۟; human security fails exactly outside its reckoning.
أَمْ حَسِبَ ... أَن لَّن يُخْرِجَ ٱللَّهُ أَضْغَٰنَهُمْ makes the false "hasiba an lan" concern what people think God will never expose.
وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَٰفِلًا عَمَّا يَعْمَلُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ directly rejects the thought that oppressive deeds have escaped the divine witness.
The record leaves neither small nor great إِلَّآ أَحْصَىٰهَا; exact divine counting corrects the man's count of wealth and his belief that no one saw.
أَحْصَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُ وَنَسُوهُ contrasts God's complete count of deeds with human forgetting, and closes by calling God witness over everything.
وَأَحْصَىٰ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ عَدَدًۢا states the real counting behind the section's contrast between حساب as enumeration and حسب as supposition.
The just balances omit nothing, even a mustard seed, and وَكَفَىٰ بِنَا حَٰسِبِينَ identifies God as the sufficient reckoner.
إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ حَسِيبًا extends حساب from human counting to the One who takes account of every thing.
كَفَىٰ بِنَفْسِكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكَ حَسِيبًا turns the final record into an account the person himself cannot deny.
ٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ بِحُسْبَانٍ presents حساب as exact ordered calculation rather than the man's unfounded guess.
ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّىٰكَ فَعَدَلَكَ depicts the human as created, proportioned, and balanced—the body as fitted work.
فِىٓ أَىِّ صُورَةٍ مَّا شَآءَ رَكَّبَكَ completes 82:7 by describing the bodily form as an intentionally assembled shape.
ثُمَّ سَوَّىٰهُ ... وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَٱلْأَبْصَٰرَ وَٱلْأَفْـِٔدَةَ parallels the section's measured organs with proportioning followed by جعل.
God brings humans from wombs unknowing and جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَٱلْأَبْصَٰرَ وَٱلْأَفْـِٔدَةَ, making faculties gifts fitted to the newborn.
وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنشَأَ لَكُمُ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَٱلْأَبْصَٰرَ وَٱلْأَفْـِٔدَةَ is a direct counterpart to eyes, tongue, and lips as created parts.
هُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنشَأَكُمْ وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَٱلْأَبْصَٰرَ وَٱلْأَفْـِٔدَةَ attributes both the human and his faculties to one Maker.
إِنَّا خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَانَ ... فَجَعَلْنَٰهُ سَمِيعًۢا بَصِيرًا directly joins خلق and جعل in the purposeful making of sensory capacities.
جَعَلْنَا لَهُمْ سَمْعًا وَأَبْصَٰرًا وَأَفْـِٔدَةً names the fitted faculties, then shows they avail nothing when God's signs are denied.
The One who created the heavens and earth is asked أَوَلَيْسَ ... بِقَٰدِرٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يَخْلُقَ مِثْلَهُم; creation establishes power to recreate.
The people are asked whether the Creator of the heavens and earth is بِقَٰدِرٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يُحْـِۧىَ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ, exposing their false boundary on divine power.
The ayah joins خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ, power to create humans again, and a جَعَلَ fixed term, uniting craft, ability, and limit.
Creation of the seven heavens and earth culminates in knowing أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ and that His knowledge encompasses every thing.
وَمَا قَدَرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِۦ names the human failure to estimate God, then the earth in His grasp displays the power their measure missed.
وَمَا قَدَرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِۦ ... إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَقَوِىٌّ عَزِيزٌ directly opposes faulty human estimation to divine strength.
وَمَا قَدَرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِۦ identifies denial of revelation as failure to measure God truly, another form of setting a false limit on Him.
In the layered heavens مَّا تَرَىٰ فِى خَلْقِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ مِن تَفَٰوُتٍ: created work bears no mismatch, the cosmic form of straight proportion.
لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَانَ فِىٓ أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ makes the human's creation an excellent setting-straight, close to the section's measured bodily pattern.
هُوَ ٱلَّذِى يُصَوِّرُكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْحَامِ كَيْفَ يَشَآءُ locates deliberate bodily formation in the womb and attributes it to the one irresistible God.
خَلَقَكُم ... ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا and خَلْقًا مِّنۢ بَعْدِ خَلْقٍ in three womb-darknesses join creation, making, generation, and divine kingship.
Divine stores descend only بِقَدَرٍ مَّعْلُومٍ, presenting provision itself as a known measured portion.
God withholds unlimited provision lest people transgress and يُنَزِّلُ بِقَدَرٍ, making measure purposeful rather than humiliating.
وَمَن قُدِرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقُهُ gives the section's exact narrowed-provision construction and commands spending from what God gave within that limit.
ٱللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيَقْدِرُ places expansion and restriction with God, while its recipients rejoice wrongly in the nearer life.
God يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ and is خَبِيرًۢا بَصِيرًا, joining measured provision to the seeing knowledge denied by the boastful man.
After Qarun's fall, observers learn that God يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ and that their earlier wish for his allotment misread its meaning.
ٱللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ لَهُ makes differing livelihood an act of the One who knows every thing.
أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ asks people to see that God expands provision and يَقْدِرُ, answering both false interpretation and imagined lack of witness.
قُلْ إِنَّ رَبِّى يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ answers the wealthy speakers of 34:35: abundance is allocation, not proof against punishment.
God يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ لَهُ and replaces what is spent, tying measured share to the man's boast about expenditure.
أَوَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوٓا۟ asks whether they know that God expands provision and يَقْدِرُ; the alternation is a sign, not their private verdict.
The One who owns the keys of heaven and earth يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ, grounding allotment in encompassing knowledge and ownership.
How could God have a child without a consort when وَخَلَقَ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ? The ayah explicitly distinguishes the Creator of every thing from generated parenthood.
مَا كَانَ لِلَّهِ أَن يَتَّخِذَ مِن وَلَدٍ separates the One from offspring, while His decree "Be" identifies creation rather than begetting as His act.
God has taken no child and has no co-god; otherwise each deity would take بِمَا خَلَقَ and seek to overpower the other, joining creation to exclusive power.
The denial that God takes a child ends هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْوَٰحِدُ ٱلْقَهَّارُ, connecting the One beyond generation with irresistible power.
فَمَا مِنكُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حَٰجِزِينَ says no one could shield even the messenger from divine seizure if he fabricated words, reversing human invulnerability.
God shares His judgment with وَلَا يُشْرِكُ فِى حُكْمِهِۦٓ أَحَدًا; the negative أَحَد belongs properly to exclusive divine rule.
Messengers لَا يَخْشَوْنَ أَحَدًا إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ and God is sufficient حَسِيبًا, bringing "no one but God" together with the true reckoner.
وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُعْجِزَهُۥ مِن شَىْءٍ denies that anything can defeat God's reach and grounds it in His knowledge and power.
When God intends harm فَلَا مَرَدَّ لَهُۥ and there is no protector besides Him, setting a firm boundary against the thought of being unreachable.
وَمَآ أَنتُم بِمُعْجِزِينَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ denies every location from which humans might frustrate God.
وَمَآ أَنتُم بِمُعْجِزِينَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ and the absence of any protector or helper overturn the man's confidence that none can master him.
Who is the army that could help مِن دُونِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ? The rhetorical question exposes confidence in independent protection as delusion.
Who could provide if God withheld His provision? This reverses the recipient's claim over his share and returns rizq to the One who measures it.
If God touches a person with harm no one removes it but Him, and وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ states the power excluded by the man's boast.
تِلْكَ إِذًا قِسْمَةٌ ضِيزَىٰ condemns the idolaters' division as unjust, a boundary between human partition and right apportionment.
They أَقْسَمُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ that God will not raise the dead; their oath embodies a false human estimate of divine power that God's promise reverses.
وَتَحْسَبُونَهُۥ هَيِّنًا وَهُوَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ عَظِيمٌ contrasts human assessment with God's, showing that حسب can badly mismeasure a deed.
وَقَالُوا۟ نَحْنُ أَكْثَرُ أَمْوَٰلًا وَأَوْلَٰدًا وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمُعَذَّبِينَ voices the wealth-and-power inference that measured provision in 34:36 corrects.
Qarun says إِنَّمَآ أُوتِيتُهُۥ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ عِندِى, claiming his huge share as the product of his own calculation despite stronger predecessors destroyed by God.
When the earth swallows Qarun, no faction can help him and he cannot help himself, the enacted reversal of wealth-based invulnerability before 28:82 names provision's true allocator.
The garden owner is taught to say مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِٱللَّهِ, replacing confidence in his estate with the admission that power belongs to God.
After the garden's loss he has no group to help him besides God وَمَا كَانَ مُنتَصِرًا, a concrete end to the belief that one's holdings secure power.
فَٱلْمُقَسِّمَٰتِ أَمْرًا evokes agents distributing the commanded affair, a likely instance of قسم as apportionment behind the section's oath-word.
Men and women each have نَصِيبًا مَّفْرُوضًا from an estate; this legally fixed share makes concrete the section's definition of a portion measured for each person.
When dependants, orphans, and the poor attend ٱلْقِسْمَةَ, they too are to be provided, joining division of property to responsibility for one's share.
وَلِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنَا ... فَـَٔاتُوهُمْ نَصِيبَهُمْ brings "for each," جعل, and an owed share together under God's witness.
People يَجْعَلُونَ ... نَصِيبًا from God's provision for what they do not know, another invented share that will be questioned.
إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِٱلْمِرْصَادِ places the Lord on watch over the powerful peoples just named, preparing the correction of human readings of wealth in 89:15-16.
كَلَّا بَل لَّا تُكْرِمُونَ ٱلْيَتِيمَ rejects the human verdict about honor and redirects the meaning of provision toward what he does with the vulnerable.
Failure to urge feeding the poor shows that a measured share carries a social claim, completing the correction begun after 89:16.
وَتَأْكُلُونَ ٱلتُّرَاثَ أَكْلًا لَّمًّا depicts inherited portions being swallowed indiscriminately, the corrupt human handling of division.
وَتُحِبُّونَ ٱلْمَالَ حُبًّا جَمًّا names the attachment that makes humans read their allotted wealth as personal rank and power.
مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنِّى مَالِيَهْ is the final admission that accumulated wealth did not make its possessor self-sufficient.
هَلَكَ عَنِّى سُلْطَٰنِيَهْ adds that his authority has vanished too, completing the collapse of imagined wealth and power.
أَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّمَا نُمِدُّهُم بِهِۦ مِن مَّالٍ وَبَنِينَ asks whether recipients suppose wealth and sons have the meaning they assign to them.
نُسَارِعُ لَهُمْ فِى ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ rejects that supposition: an enlarged share is not itself a verdict of favor.
إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ لَا يَرْجُونَ حِسَابًا identifies refusal to expect an account as the posture behind acting as though no one can measure one's deeds.
وَكُلَّ شَىْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَٰهُ كِتَٰبًا answers 78:27 with a complete written count, opposed to human denial of reckoning.
لَّقَدْ أَحْصَىٰهُمْ وَعَدَّهُمْ عَدًّا says every servant has been encompassed and counted exactly, leaving no anonymous "no one" outside the One's knowledge.
وَكُلُّهُمْ ءَاتِيهِ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ فَرْدًا gives the consequence of 19:94: each measured person comes to God alone.
ٱلَّذِىٓ أَحْسَنَ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلَقَهُۥ describes created things as well-made work, supporting the artisan sense of خلق developed in the section.
God صَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ and provided good things, joining fitted bodily form to provision.
خَلَقَ ... بِٱلْحَقِّ وَصَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ treats the human form as part of purposeful creation, not self-owned material.
صُنْعَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَتْقَنَ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ names God's making as work perfected in every thing, a nonlexical parallel to straight, exact measure.
Water is sent from the sky بِقَدَرٍ and revives dead land, another concrete provision whose amount and effect are measured.
وَكَانَ أَمْرُ ٱللَّهِ قَدَرًا مَّقْدُورًا expresses divine command as an appointed measure carried to its destined end.
عَلَى ٱلْمُوسِعِ قَدَرُهُۥ وَعَلَى ٱلْمُقْتِرِ قَدَرُهُۥ makes a gift proportionate to each person's capacity, a practical instance of measured portion.
Rain sends valleys flowing بِقَدَرِهَا, so each channel receives according to its capacity; this concretizes measure as a thing's extent and limit.
The sun's course is تَقْدِيرُ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْعَلِيمِ, a visible created motion governed by the powerful Knower's determination.
وَٱلْقَمَرَ قَدَّرْنَٰهُ مَنَازِلَ continues 36:38 with measured lunar stages, making determination a sequence of bounded stations.
Silver vessels قَدَّرُوهَا تَقْدِيرًا are proportioned to measure, a material crafting scene that echoes measuring the hide to its intended form.
ثُمَّ نَظَرَ continues "he thought and measured" with the looking-into-the-matter named in the section's dictionary gloss for human taqdīr.
مِنْ أَىِّ شَىْءٍ خَلَقَهُۥ opens the 80:19 creation-and-measure claim by confronting the human with the material from which he was made.
ثُمَّ ٱلسَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُۥ follows measured creation with an eased way, paralleling the section's sequence from creating and determining to guiding the two paths.
ثُمَّ أَمَاتَهُۥ فَأَقْبَرَهُۥ gives the measured human his mortal endpoint, which his self-calculation cannot prevent.
ثُمَّ إِذَا شَآءَ أَنشَرَهُۥ completes the sequence after 80:19 by placing resurrection under the Creator's will and power.
فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلْغَمِّ supplies the result of Jonah's call in 21:87: return to God, rather than presumed escape from His measure, brings rescue.
فَلْيَنظُرِ ٱلْإِنسَانُ مِمَّ خُلِقَ commands the human to examine his own created origin before supposing himself beyond power.
خُلِقَ مِن مَّآءٍ دَافِقٍ answers 86:5 with the lowly material from which the apparently self-sufficient human was crafted.
The fluid's bodily emergence makes 86:6 a concrete generative scene, not an abstract assertion of creation.
إِنَّهُۥ عَلَىٰ رَجْعِهِۦ لَقَادِرٌ turns the first creation into proof of power to return the human.
يَوْمَ تُبْلَى ٱلسَّرَآئِرُ adds that concealed things will be exposed, answering the supposition that no one saw.
The full sequence from dust and drop through womb, birth, maturity, and death makes bodily creation a measured progression to an appointed term and evidence for resurrection.
وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَانَ مِن سُلَٰلَةٍ مِّن طِينٍ begins a workshop-like account of the human's material formation.
ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَٰهُ نُطْفَةً فِى قَرَارٍ مَّكِينٍ joins جعل to the fitted placement of the created human in the womb.
Successive bodily forms culminate in خَلْقًا ءَاخَرَ and أَحْسَنُ ٱلْخَٰلِقِينَ, making creation an ordered transformation of material.
God خَلَقَ humans from weakness, جَعَلَ strength and later weakness, and closes وَهُوَ ٱلْعَلِيمُ ٱلْقَدِيرُ; a whole life is shaped within His power.
Creation from dust and a drop, conception and birth by God's knowledge, and every extended or shortened life written down present generation and lifespan as measured together.
The human passes by God's creating through dust, drop, clot, birth, maturity, old age, and an appointed term, a direct anatomy of measure as an endpoint.
أَمْ خُلِقُوا۟ مِنْ غَيْرِ شَىْءٍ أَمْ هُمُ ٱلْخَٰلِقُونَ confronts humans with the impossible alternatives of being unmade or being their own makers.
أَمْ خَلَقُوا۟ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ extends 52:35 from self-creation to cosmic power and locates the error in their lack of certainty.
وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَٰكُمْ ثُمَّ صَوَّرْنَٰكُمْ explicitly follows creation with bodily shaping, matching the section's sense of material cut to form.
أَتَعْبُدُونَ مَا تَنْحِتُونَ introduces literal human carving, a concrete craft against which the Creator's work is distinguished.
وَٱللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ وَمَا تَعْمَلُونَ answers the carving scene by placing both the artisans and their work under God's creation.
God owns the dominion, يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُ, and bestows daughters or sons as He wills; offspring are apportioned gifts, not human possession.
God combines sons and daughters or يَجْعَلُ مَن يَشَآءُ عَقِيمًا and closes عَلِيمٌ قَدِيرٌ, joining reproductive share, جعل, knowledge, and power.
وَأَنَّهُۥ خَلَقَ ٱلزَّوْجَيْنِ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلْأُنثَىٰ attributes the two sexes in the begetting scene to one Creator.
مِن نُّطْفَةٍ إِذَا تُمْنَىٰ gives 53:45 its generative material, keeping created sex and human procreation distinct.
وَأَنَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلنَّشْأَةَ ٱلْأُخْرَىٰ carries the Creator's ownership of first formation into the second creation.
مَّا خَلْقُكُمْ وَلَا بَعْثُكُمْ إِلَّا كَنَفْسٍ وَٰحِدَةٍ makes the creation and resurrection of all humanity one act to the God who hears and sees.
مِن قَبْلِ أَن تَقْدِرُوا۟ عَلَيْهِمْ uses the same قدر على construction for gaining power over persons, confirming the section's lexical sense of mastery in a human legal setting.
The owned servant لَا يَقْدِرُ عَلَىٰ شَىْءٍ is contrasted with one given good provision who spends from it, placing ability, ownership, allotted rizq, and expenditure in one parable.
أَنَّ ٱلْمَآءَ قِسْمَةٌۢ بَيْنَهُمْ makes water an apportioned share between the people and the she-camel, a direct scene of قسم as division.
لِكُلِّ بَابٍ مِّنْهُمْ جُزْءٌ مَّقْسُومٌ gives each gate an assigned portion, concretely combining "for each," part, and division.
تَقَاسَمُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ turns the oath-root into a collectively measured plan to attack Ṣāliḥ's household and then control the account of what happened.
وَمَكَرُوا۟ مَكْرًا وَمَكَرْنَا مَكْرًا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ sets the conspirators' calculation against a divine plan they do not perceive.
Their destruction is the visible outcome of 27:49-50, showing how completely their sworn estimate of power failed.
They أَقْسَمُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ that a warner would make them better guided, but his arrival increases aversion; oath and claimed guidance expose a false self-measure.
أَوَلَمْ تَكُونُوٓا۟ أَقْسَمْتُم ... مَا لَكُم مِّن زَوَالٍ recalls an oath that they would never pass away, joining قسم to denial of the appointed limit.
At the Hour criminals يُقْسِمُ ... مَا لَبِثُوا۟ غَيْرَ سَاعَةٍ; their oath embodies a false measurement of elapsed time even at judgment.
وَبَدَا لَهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَمْ يَكُونُوا۟ يَحْتَسِبُونَ says divine judgment discloses what their reckoning never included.
The thirsty person يَحْسَبُهُ ٱلظَّمْـَٔانُ مَآءً follows a false visual estimate to its endpoint, where he finds God and receives his full حساب.
إِنَّمَا نَعُدُّ لَهُمْ عَدًّا says God is counting out the wrongdoers' remaining time, a precise reversal of their impatience and imagined freedom.
وَكُلَّ شَىْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَٰهُ فِىٓ إِمَامٍ مُّبِينٍ sets every act and trace within a complete divine count.
وَإِن تَعُدُّوا۟ نِعْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَا contrasts human inability to enumerate divine gifts with the boastful man's count of wealth.
وَإِن تَعُدُّوا۟ نِعْمَةَ ٱللَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَا repeats the boundary on human counting in a passage about God's manifold provisions.
أَحَسِبَ ٱلنَّاسُ أَن يُتْرَكُوٓا۟ asks whether people suppose they will be left merely on their claim of faith, paralleling the thought of being left untested and unbounded.
أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أَن تُتْرَكُوا۟ rejects the supposition that people are simply left before their loyalties become known to God.
أَمْ حَسِبَ ... أَن نَّجْعَلَهُمْ كَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ exposes a human calculation that wrongly assigns equal outcomes, placing حسب against God's just جعل.
They swear to God as they swore to people وَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ عَلَىٰ شَىْءٍ; oath and supposition combine in an empty claim to standing.
وَهُمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ يُحْسِنُونَ صُنْعًا identifies the greatest losers by a mistaken assessment of their own making.
وَلَا يَسْتَثْنُونَ shows the garden owners made their sworn harvest plan without reserving it to God's will, clarifying their presumed control.
A visitation from the Lord circles the garden while they sleep, inserting divine power into the calculation they thought complete.
أَنَا۠ أَكْثَرُ مِنكَ مَالًا وَأَعَزُّ نَفَرًا voices the wealthy man's count of assets and supporters as a claim to superior power.
مَآ أَظُنُّ أَن تَبِيدَ هَٰذِهِۦٓ أَبَدًا turns counted wealth into a false supposition that the garden has no limit.
His companion answers with the One who خَلَقَكَ مِن تُرَابٍ ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ سَوَّىٰكَ رَجُلًا, opposing the boast with created, proportioned origin.
The fruit is encompassed and its owner wrings his hands over what he spent, an enacted reversal of his estimate that the garden could not perish.
إِنَّمَا ٱللَّهُ إِلَٰهٌ وَٰحِدٌ ... أَن يَكُونَ لَهُۥ وَلَدٌ explicitly joins divine oneness to transcendence beyond having a child.
وَمَا يَنۢبَغِى لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ أَن يَتَّخِذَ وَلَدًا sets a firm boundary between the Creator and generated offspring.
Every being in heaven and earth comes to the Merciful only as a servant, supplying the creature–Creator relation that replaces divine parenthood.
تَعَٰلَىٰ جَدُّ رَبِّنَا مَا ٱتَّخَذَ صَٰحِبَةً وَلَا وَلَدًا places the exalted Lord outside spouse and offspring.
Floodwaters meet عَلَىٰٓ أَمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِرَ, giving ق د ر the sense of an event already carried to its appointed outcome.
ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ adds absolute recourse and sufficiency to the One of 112:1, sharpening the contrast with a created man's imagined self-sufficiency.
The human once passed through a span when he was not a thing mentioned, preparing 76:2's claim that his hearing and sight are made rather than self-possessed.
وَلَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا gives each soul a bounded capacity, while the truthful record prevents that measure from becoming arbitrary.
قُلْ هَلْ نُنَبِّئُكُم بِٱلْأَخْسَرِينَ أَعْمَٰلًا introduces 18:104's people whose self-measure of their work is opposite to its real outcome.
وَمَآ أَمْوَٰلُكُمْ وَلَآ أَوْلَٰدُكُم بِٱلَّتِى تُقَرِّبُكُمْ rejects wealth and children as measures of nearness, completing the correction of 34:35-36.
Qarun's display makes people who desire the nearer life wish for مِثْلَ مَآ أُوتِىَ قَٰرُونُ, showing how spectators misread another's allotted share.
Those given knowledge call God's reward better, supplying the correct counter-measure to the worldly wish in 28:79 before Qarun's fall.
وَمَا مِنَّآ إِلَّا لَهُۥ مَقَامٌ مَّعْلُومٌ gives every angel a known station, an indirect instance of a portion or limit assigned to each.
Men and women each have نَصِيبٌۭ مِّمَّا ٱكْتَسَبُوا۟, while envy is redirected toward asking God's bounty; shares are received within divine apportionment.
The seeker of the world receives some of it but has no نَصِيبٍ in the hereafter, a non-خلاق formulation of the section's measured share and its horizon.
God has preferred some over others in provision, while those favored resist making dependants equal partners in it; the ayah probes ownership of an allotted share.
ٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ فَضَّلْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ asks the reader to observe differentiated shares and says the hereafter has still greater ranks.
The claim that God took a child is answered هُوَ ٱلْغَنِىُّ and by His ownership of all things, locating true self-sufficiency with the Creator.
The earth yields مِن كُلِّ شَىْءٍ مَّوْزُونٍ, a nonlexical parallel in which created growth comes in balanced measure.
God raises heaven وَوَضَعَ ٱلْمِيزَانَ, making balance part of the created order rather than a human invention.
أَلَّا تَطْغَوْا۟ فِى ٱلْمِيزَانِ turns the given measure into a boundary humans must not overrun.
وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلْوَزْنَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ commands humans to make their own measuring straight and not diminish the balance.
